narrative.overview:
Vyom ERP delivers an authoritative, high-density industrial control room experience purpose-built for the rigorous fabrication of custom electrical control panels. The interface balances high-throughput technical scanning with uncompromising engineering safety gates. Rather than treating panel manufacturing as generic inventory rows, the design language communicates physical manufacturing status with clarity across busy shop floors and engineering desks.

The aesthetic is anchored by deep obsidian and dark slate surfaces (#0b0f19 to #243048), establishing a high-contrast visual substrate where status indicators pierce through high-ambient shop-floor illumination. Semantic neon accents (electric flame orange, high-voltage sky blue, pass-rate emerald, and fault crimson) serve as unequivocal telemetry signals, allowing engineers and shop supervisors to diagnose bottlenecks, holds, and approvals at a glance.
keyCharacteristics: High-Density Data Instrumentation: Dense, tightly aligned tabular and Gantt views that maximize visible serials and line items per viewport without nested navigation.
Uncompromising Visual Gates: Blocked states, missing engineering documents (Drawing & BOM), and hold conditions are rendered with unmistakable high-visibility contrast.
Tonal Depth & Crisp Boundaries: Layers are separated by subtle surface stepping and 1px technical borders (#1e293b), avoiding distracting heavy drop shadows.

Dual Type Personality: Humanist precision typography (Plus Jakarta Sans) for operational text paired with technical monospaced telemetry (IBM Plex Mono) for all order numbers, serial IDs, part numbers, and timestamps.

rules.name: The Rarity of Flame Rule
rules.body: The primary accent (#f97316) is strictly reserved for user focus and critical forward progress. It must never coat decorative surfaces or exceed 10% of any viewport.

rules.name: The Unambiguous Status Rule
rules.body: Every operational status badge must combine distinct hue, a 12% opacity tint container, and an explicit text label (never rely on color alone).

rules.name: The Monospace Serial Rule
rules.body: All order numbers (YY(YY+1)XXXX), unit serial numbers, line item tags, part numbers, and financial-year identifiers must be rendered in var(--font-mono) (IBM Plex Mono) to guarantee column alignment and unmistakable character differentiation.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Cards and table rows are flat at rest. Elevation and subtle ambient glows (rgba(56, 189, 248, 0.15)) appear strictly as interactive feedback during hover, selection, or modal focus.

dos: Do use IBM Plex Mono for all serial numbers, order numbers, part numbers, and timestamps.
Do enforce high contrast for all status badges (pair icon + color + text label).
Do preserve 1px technical borders between dark layers to maintain clarity on low-end shop-floor displays.
Do display mandatory gates (PO upload, Drawing & BOM presence, Design confirmation) prominently before action buttons.
Do support keyboard Escape closing behavior across all modals and slide-out drawers via useGlobalModalEscape.
donts: Don't use diffuse multi-colored drop shadows that muddy dark industrial interfaces.
Don't use generic un-scoped colors outside the calibrated CSS token system.
Don't hide critical order identifiers or manufacturing statuses behind multi-level hover tooltips; prioritize scannable inline chips.
Don't allow UI actions that bypass upstream engineering gates.
